A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ShorterBetter and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original model-training evaluations, reasoning-trace analyses, and reward-design ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds human annotation validation, hyperparameter sensitivity results, another ablation, and Llama-8B experiments.

M1.justification: The shortest-correct-response SOL, average-length fallback, correctness-plus-length reward, and GRPO optimization remain unchanged. The Llama experiment applies the existing method to another backbone without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same dataset and task coverage. The added sensitivity and Llama experiments use existing benchmarks, and human verification examines existing AMC reasoning traces. These additions change configurations and analyses rather than represented tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B as the unmodified baseline for the new Llama-based ShorterBetter model. Existing Qwen, Instruct, Training Efficient, O1-Pruner, and Marco-o1 comparisons remain. L1 and ConciseR receive discussion but no reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: v4 substantially extends experimental conditions: Appendix B.5 adds Llama-8B training for 100 steps with alpha=5; Appendix A.4 tests alpha=0.1 and 5 beyond the earlier 1/2 settings; Section 5.2 introduces manual validation covering 49 AMC problems and 2,064 sentences. Existing Qwen training and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds an ablation retaining correctness reward while always targeting the shortest response, a wider alpha sensitivity study, and human verification of automated reasoning labels. Appendix B.5 also tests dependence on the model backbone. These materially expand checks on reward design, annotation reliability, and generalization.

E5.justification: Reporting remains based on point estimates. The new human–LLM agreement percentages are validation outcomes; v4 adds no repeated-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 6 add human-validation, alpha-sensitivity, and Llama results, alongside expanded ablation curves. Human–LLM agreement is reported as 94.23% by sentence and 93.01% by token. The new Llama comparison reports LiveCodeBench accuracy of 0.54 versus 0.37 and lengths of 8,101 versus 1,665 tokens for base versus trained models. Original Qwen benchmark values are retained.

T1.justification: The OL and SOL definitions, reward equation, GRPO objective and detailed expressions, and AE-score formulation are unchanged. Added hyperparameter explanations and related-work arguments introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: autonomous SOL-guided reasoning compression, 50–80% length reduction for the Qwen-based models while maintaining accuracy, and improved reasoning-trace structure.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of human-label disagreements and alpha-dependent accuracy/compression tradeoffs. Appendix B.5 acknowledges greater out-of-domain accuracy losses for Llama and suggests fewer training steps or larger alpha. These qualify and extend the discussion while retaining the original interpretation of the Qwen results.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports releasing an annotation tool and human-labeled data. Appendix A.4 adds practical tuning guidance, including starting with alpha in [2,5]. Existing training software, GPU counts, training times, judge settings, and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix C adds ConciseR and expands comparison with L1, distinguishing SOL-based autonomous optimization from staged compression and explicit budgets. The Gemini reference is corrected. Most remaining citation changes update publication metadata for existing works rather than introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with localized explanatory additions and a new related-work appendix. Earlier Appendices C/D become D/E. Equal-contribution, acknowledgment, and conference information are added, although the appendix contents list retains stale C/D labels.

P2.justification: v4 adds three tables and separates the earlier two-panel ablation figure into the retained alpha=0 panel and an expanded, redrawn collapse plot with revised legends and axes. Appendix figures and tables move and receive new numbers; the overall visual design and other existing plots remain stable.

improvement.justification: Human verification, the added reward-design control, and the alpha sweep provide useful support missing from v3; the Llama experiment also documents limits to accuracy preservation. The improvement is bounded: human verification covers only ShorterBetter-7B on AMC, and Appendix C's new efficiency advantages over ConciseR are asserted without direct experimental comparison.
